Tessa / Marcus — did a quick pass against their numbers. High-level guidance and three concrete configs below. I attached the raw calc (internal_sku_calc.csv).

Summary of SKU tradeoffs (brief):
- H100 (80GB, HBM): Best for large-context 70B-class models and lowest latency for heavy KV/cache footprints. Higher $/hour and larger power footprint. Best when you need single-GPU 70B serving or want fewer nodes for high-concurrency 70B.
- A100 (40GB or 80GB variants): Good balance for 34B and some 70B splits (model sharding) if you can accept slightly higher tail latency. 80GB A100 is typically better for 34B single-GPU and for efficient multi-GPU splits. More mature ecosystem and slightly lower cost than H100.
- L4 (48GB vRAM inference-optimized): Extremely cost-effective for 7B–13B family (quantized). Great for POC/scale-out cheap path; not ideal for 70B or large context sizes; lower single-request latency for small models and high throughput per dollar.

Assumptions used (from their forecast + our latency budget):
- Avg tokens/request: 80 tokens.
- Target user qps steady: 120 qps; peaks 450 qps; assume 25% of requests require the full model (others can be cached or routed to a smaller model).
- Candidate models: 13B quantized (L4-friendly), 34B quantized (A100 80GB ok), 70B fp16/quantized (H100 strongly preferred).

Config A — POC (quick, low-cost): L4 pool
- Model: 13B quantized; batch strategy: dynamic batching, max batch 96 (for 80-token avg).
- SKU: L4 (48GB) — baseline throughput ~600 tokens/sec per GPU (estim from our bench for 13B quant). For avg 80 tokens/request -> ~7.5 req/sec per GPU -> ~540 req/sec per 10 GPUs.
- Proposed pool: 4 L4 GPUs for initial POC (handles burst and gives headroom); cost: ~reserved equivalent $Xk/month (see calc).
- Notes: Fast to provision (supported on Dedicated), low risk. Use as warm path for quick responses and fall back to A100/H100 for complex cases.

Config B — Canary/Min Prod (balanced): A100 80GB pool + L4 warmers
- Model: 34B quant (or 13B fallback). A100 80GB throughput for 34B ~320 tokens/sec per GPU (approx). -> ~4 req/sec per GPU at 80 tokens.
- To meet steady 120 qps: need ~30 A100 GPUs raw. With autoscale and 2.5x safety margin for peaks and cold cache -> recommend reserved pool of 75 A100 GPUs (this looks large because their peaks are high; see notes below for optimizations).
- To reduce A100 count: offload 60% of traffic to L4 13B for simple queries, maintain A100 for complex/long-context calls.
- Cost: materially higher than L4-only; better latency vs model size tradeoff than multi-node 70B.

Config C — Production latency-first (70B path): H100 80GB + A100 warmers
- Model: 70B (fp16 or q4f16), single-GPU serving on H100 for best latency. H100 token/sec for 70B ~220 tokens/sec (~2.75 req/sec at 80 tokens).
- To service 120 steady qps: need ~44 H100 GPUs raw; with 2.5x buffer and targeted canary -> recommended reserved pool of 100 H100 GPUs for full production (again, initial prod may be smaller depending on traffic split).
- This is expensive but reduces cross-GPU communication and simplifies correctness for large contexts.

Operational guidance / optimizations to reduce GPU footprint:
- Intelligent routing: route short/simple requests to L4 13B; route long-context or high-accuracy to 34B/70B. If 60% can be served by L4, A100/H100 counts drop by ~60%.
- Prefix/KV cache: for repetitive patterns, caching can reduce per-token generation by 20–40% in practice. Warm caches should live on the same pool where possible.
- Quantization: using q4f16 / q5 variants reduces memory and allows larger batch sizes, especially on L4/A100. H100 still best for fp16 70B.
- Autoscale & burst: keep small reserved pool for baseline and use cloud burst (if contract allows) for short peaks. For Dedicated, recommend reserved + limited burst agreement.
- Rollouts: start POC on L4; measure hit-rates and move canary traffic to A100; evaluate H100 only if 70B accuracy delta justifies cost.

Quick numbers excerpt (rounded):
- L4 13B quant: ~600 tok/s -> ~7.5 req/s per GPU -> cost per req low.
- A100 80GB 34B quant: ~320 tok/s -> ~4 req/s per GPU.
- H100 80GB 70B fp16: ~220 tok/s -> ~2.75 req/s per GPU.

Sizing formula I used (simple):
required_gpus = ceil((peak_qps * avg_tokens_per_req / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu) * safety_margin)
where safety_margin=2.5 for production planning and 1.2 for POC.

Examples using their numbers (peak 450 qps, avg 80 tokens):
- L4 POC (safety 1.2): tokens/sec demand = 450 * 80 = 36k tok/s -> /600 => 60 GPUs (peak!) but POC steady at 120 qps -> ~14 GPUs. So 4 for baseline POC gives headroom for testing but expect degraded perf at peak.
- A100 (for 34B) production 450 qps -> tokens/sec 36k -> /320 => 113 GPUs raw -> *2.5 => 283 reserved (huge), so routing & caching critical to cut this.

Recommendation (practical):
1) POC (3 weeks): 4x L4 + 2x A100 warmers for benchmarking 34B flows. Validate routing % and cache hit rates.
2) Canary: after POC, run mixed pool: L4 fleet (10–20 GPUs) + A100 fleet sized to observed offload (~10–30 GPUs).
3) Prod: if accuracy requires 70B for a significant fraction, evaluate H100 pools. Otherwise optimize for mix of L4 + A100.

Next steps: I'll prepare a small benchmark script and run local perf tests against their sample payloads. If agreed, I can propose reserved pool sizes with cost estimates for 12-month reserved pricing.

Hi Priya / team,

Thanks for the details and the cost model — we've sketched a practical approach that balances speed-to-POC and a path to production without overprovisioning up front. High-level recommendation:

- POC (fast, low-cost): Start on L4 with a small pool (we recommend 4x L4 GPUs). This will let you validate integration, prompt engineering, and routing policies quickly. L4 is much cheaper and suitable for a 13B quantized model which handles the majority of short/structured requests.

- Canary / early production: Run a mixed pool. Keep L4s as the warm/fast path and add A100 80GB nodes for the heavier 34B flows. For initial canary, we suggest: 10–20 L4 + 6–12 A100 80GB (we'll refine after we see traffic split). This keeps costs controlled while providing headroom for medium complexity requests.

- Production (latency/accuracy critical): If you determine a material portion of your traffic requires 70B (or very large context windows), the H100 80GB is the right choice. H100s reduce inter-GPU comms and improve single-request latency for 70B-class models, but at a higher cost. Consider a hybrid long-term strategy: L4 for easy/predictable traffic, A100 for mid-sized heavy usage, H100 only where 70B is essential.
